Derive the pressure distribution inside a centrifuge by integrating the radial force balance dP/dr = ρ·r·ω², yielding the general formula P(r) = P₀ + ½ρω²(r² − r₀²).
Express ω in rad/s by converting 10,000 RPM using ω = 10,000 × 2π/60, giving ω ≈ 1047.2 rad/s.
Keep ρ, r_inner, r_outer, P₀, and r₀ as symbolic variables in the primary formula so the expression applies to any fluid and any rotor geometry.
Provide a numerical illustration using assumed values: ρ = 1000 kg/m³ (water), r_inner = 0.05 m, r_outer = 0.15 m, r₀ = r_inner, and P₀ = 0 (gauge pressure at the inner wall).
Clearly label all assumed numerical values (fluid density, inner radius, outer radius, reference radius, reference pressure) as assumptions and not part of the stated requirement.
Present the final deliverable as: (1) the symbolic integrated formula P(r) = P₀ + ½ρω²(r² − r₀²) with ω = 1047.2 rad/s substituted, and (2) the numerical pressure profile evaluated at r_inner and r_outer using the stated assumptions.
Do not use the static hydrostatic formula P = ρ·g·h as the basis for the calculation; the correct approach is the integrated rotating-fluid expression where centrifugal acceleration varies with radius.
